transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I've decided to come in because I've been feeling constantly depressed and sad. It's been going on for a really long time now, about two years and one month. I just can't seem to shake this heavy mood.
Can you tell me if there have been any periods over the past two years where you felt like your depression lifted or improved for a couple of months at a time?
No, there haven't been any breaks at all. I have felt this heavy sadness consistently every single day for the last two years and a month. It hasn't lifted or gotten better even for a short time.
Have you experienced a loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you once enjoyed, or has that remained relatively intact despite your depressive feelings?
Yes, I've completely lost interest in the hobbies and activities I used to love. Even when I try to do them, I don't feel any pleasure or happiness at all, just emotionally flat and numb.
Can you describe the severity of your depressive symptoms, such as feelings of worthlessness, guilt, or suicidal thoughts, and how they impact your daily life?

I don't really experience those specific feelings of worthlessness, guilt, or suicidal thoughts. For me, it is more about a constant feeling of emptiness and having absolutely no motivation to do anything.
Do you also experience any symptoms of anxiety, such as excessive worry, fear, or panic, in addition to your depressive symptoms?
No, I haven't really noticed those kinds of feelings. I don't really experience anxiety, excessive worry, or panic.
Can you confirm if your depressive symptoms have lasted for more than two years, which you mentioned earlier, and if they have been consistent without any significant improvement?

Yes, that's correct. My depressive symptoms have indeed lasted for about two years and one month now. They have been completely consistent and persistent, without any noticeable improvement at all during this entire period.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms have lasted for more than two years with no significant improvement, and they experience a consistent feeling of sadness and loss of interest in activities. This long duration and consistency of symptoms, without any periods of improvement, align more closely with the criteria for Persistent Depressive Disorder. Major Depressive Disorder typically involves one or more major depressive episodes, which may not be the case here given the patient's description of a continuous, unrelenting depressive state without mention of discrete episodes or significant variability in symptom severity. Therefore, Persistent Depressive Disorder becomes the more likely candidate based on the information provided.
